newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas holds late gains, opinions mixed.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas holds late gains, opinions mixed.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures held modest gains late Monday in sluggish trade, but most agreed there was little conviction about market direction during this holiday-shortened week, industry sources said.
At 1415 EST, January was 3.3 cents higher at $3.47 per million British thermal units after dipping early to $3.34. Feb was up seven cents to $3.04, while deferreds also were up.

"I think we'll have to wait until next week to get a clue. If the longer-term forecasts are for cold, we could still move up, but eventually it has to roll over and die," said one Houston-based trader.
While relatively low stocks and an uncertain winter were likely to keep the bears at bay for a while, many were cautious about getting too bullish at such historically lofty price levels.
"All the bullish news is in the price. There's not much else that can drive it right now," said an East Coast trader.
NYMEX will be closed Thursday and Friday for the U.S. Thanksgiving Day holiday.
Chartists still pegged Jan support in the mid-$3.20s and then at $3.04. Resistance was seen at the $3.68 contract high.

Cash sources said November Gulf Coast gas firmed several cents to about the $3.70 area, with December on the same pipes notionally steady in the $3.80s. Cold weather drove November Midcon prices up almost 20 cents to $3.80 or better. December Midcon gas notionally firmed 15 cents to the $3.80s. December New York city gate gas notionally was softer in the $4.80s.
NYMEX said 16,359 Hub contracts traded at 1350 EST.
NYMEX December Alberta natgas was still down by about four cents at $1.76, while deferreds were untraded at 1420 EST. NYMEX said 35 Alberta contracts traded at 1350 EST.
NYMEX December Permian natgas remained 4.5 cents higher at a new high of $3.685, while deferredss also were untraded at 1420 EST. NYMEX said 15 Permian contracts traded at 1350 EST.
NYMEX December Alberta and Permian natgas expire today.
On the KCBT, January gained four cents to $3.24, while deferreds were still steady to up three cents. The East/West spread narrowed 0.7 cent to 23.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
